Operating Characteristics of the BOIN-ET Design

Source: R/sim_boin_et.R
sim_boin_et.Rd

Simulate trials of the BOIN-ET design of Takeda, Taguri and Morita (2018) under one scenario of DLT and response probabilities, select the optimal biological dose (OBD) of each trial, and summarize how often each dose is selected and how many patients, DLTs and responses occur at each dose.

Usage

sim_boin_et(
  target,
  target_resp,
  p_true,
  p_resp,
  n_cohort,
  cohort_size,
  n_trials = 10000,
  start_dose = 1,
  n_earlystop = NULL,
  p_saf = NULL,
  p_tox = NULL,
  p_saf_resp = NULL,
  cutoff_eli = 0.95,
  cutoff_eli_resp = 0.99,
  p_eli = NULL,
  p_eli_resp = NULL,
  resp_cor = 0.2,
  resp_cor_type = c("copula", "binary"),
  boinet_compatible = FALSE,
  prior = rep(1/6, 6),
  est_method = c("observed", "multi_iso", "fp_logistic"),
  obd_method = c("max_resp", "utility_weighted", "utility_truncated_linear",
    "utility_scoring"),
  w1 = 0.33,
  w2 = 1.09,
  t_low = NULL,
  t_upp = NULL,
  e_low = NULL,
  e_upp = NULL,
  psi00 = 40,
  psi11 = 60,
  keep_trials = FALSE,
  verbose = FALSE,
  seed = 123
)

Arguments

target

Numeric scalar. Target DLT probability, for example 0.30.

target_resp

Numeric scalar. Target response probability, for example 0.60.

p_true

Numeric vector. True DLT probability at each dose level, in increasing dose order.

p_resp

Numeric vector of the same length as p_true. True response probability at each dose level.

n_cohort

Integer scalar. Number of cohorts in a trial.

cohort_size

Integer scalar or vector. Number of patients per cohort. A scalar is used for every cohort. A vector shorter than n_cohort is padded with its last element and a longer one is truncated.

n_trials

Integer scalar. Number of trials to simulate. Defaults to 10000.

start_dose

Integer scalar. Dose level for the first cohort. Defaults to 1.

n_earlystop

Integer scalar or NULL. The trial stops once this many patients have been treated at any dose. Defaults to NULL, the maximum sample size, which is the default of the 'boinet' package.

p_saf

Numeric scalar. Highest DLT probability deemed subtherapeutic. Defaults to 0.1 * target, the value recommended by Takeda et al. (2018), which is far below the 0.6 * target of the BOIN design.

p_tox

Numeric scalar. Lowest DLT probability deemed overly toxic. Defaults to 1.4 * target.

p_saf_resp

Numeric scalar. Highest response probability deemed subtherapeutic. Defaults to 0.6 * target_resp.

cutoff_eli

Numeric scalar. A dose is no longer admissible when the posterior probability that its DLT rate is below p_eli falls below 1 - cutoff_eli. Defaults to 0.95.

cutoff_eli_resp

Numeric scalar. A dose is no longer admissible when the posterior probability that its response rate is above p_eli_resp falls below 1 - cutoff_eli_resp. Defaults to 0.99.

p_eli

Numeric scalar or NULL. DLT probability of the rule above. Defaults to NULL, which uses target as the 'boinet' package does. Takeda et al. (2018) used 0.40 with a cutoff of 0.90.

p_eli_resp

Numeric scalar or NULL. Response probability of the rule above. Defaults to NULL, which uses p_saf_resp as the 'boinet' package does. Takeda et al. (2018) used 0.20 with a cutoff of 0.90.

resp_cor

Numeric scalar strictly between -1 and 1. Correlation between the DLT and the response of a patient. Defaults to 0.2, the default of the 'boinet' package.

resp_cor_type

Character scalar. How resp_cor links the two outcomes: "copula" (the default) uses it as the correlation of a Gaussian copula, which is how the 'boinet' package generates its data; "binary" uses it as the correlation of the two binary outcomes, as in the simulations of Takeda et al. (2018).

boinet_compatible

Logical scalar. Apply the rules of the 'boinet' package (version 1.6.0) exactly. Defaults to FALSE, which keeps to Takeda et al. (2018), who do not allow dose skipping during escalation; see Details.

prior

Numeric vector of length 6. Prior probabilities of the six hypotheses. Defaults to rep(1 / 6, 6), the noninformative choice of the article. The third hypothesis, under which every decision is correct, does not enter the criterion.

est_method

Character scalar. Estimator of the response rates: "observed" (the default) for the observed rates, "multi_iso" for the model-averaged unimodal isotonic regression of Lin and Yin (2017), or "fp_logistic" for the fractional polynomial logistic regression of Takeda et al. (2018), which needs the 'mfp' package.

obd_method

Character scalar. Selection rule: "max_resp" (the default) for the admissible dose with the highest estimated response rate up to the estimated MTD, or the dose that maximizes the utility "utility_weighted", "utility_truncated_linear" or "utility_scoring" among the admissible doses.

w1, w2

Numeric scalars. Weights of the weighted utility q - w1 * p - w2 * p * (p > p_tox), where p and q are the estimated DLT and response rates. Default to 0.33 and 1.09.

t_low, t_upp

Numeric scalars or NULL. DLT rates between which the truncated linear utility falls from one to zero. Default to p_saf and p_tox.

e_low, e_upp

Numeric scalars or NULL. Response rates between which the truncated linear utility rises from zero to one. Default to p_saf_resp / 2 and target_resp.

psi00, psi11

Numeric scalars. Scores of the scoring utility for a patient with neither DLT nor response and for a patient with both, the scores of a response without DLT and of a DLT without response being 100 and 0. Default to 40 and 60.

keep_trials

Logical scalar. Keep the simulated trials and the selected OBDs in the result. Defaults to FALSE.

verbose

Logical scalar. Report progress with messages. Defaults to FALSE.

seed

Integer scalar or NULL. Random seed. When NULL the current state of the random number generator is used. The state of the calling session is restored on exit. Defaults to 123.

Value

An object of class boin_et_oc, which is a list with components

design

"BOIN-ET".

target, target_resp, p_true, p_resp

The targets and the scenario.

n_doses, n_trials

Numbers of doses and of simulated trials.

lambda1, lambda2, eta1

The boundaries, see boin_et_boundary.

sel_percent

Percentage of trials selecting each dose as the OBD.

percent_no_obd

Percentage of trials selecting no OBD.

percent_early_stop

Percentage of trials stopped early.

n_pts_dose, n_tox_dose, n_resp_dose

Average numbers of patients, DLTs and responses at each dose.

total_n_pts, total_n_tox, total_n_resp

Their averages per trial.

stop_reason_percent

Percentage of trials ending for each reason, see boin_et_simulate.

est_method, obd_method

The OBD selection used.

settings

List of the design parameters.

call

The matched call.

trials, obd

The simulated trials and the selected OBDs, when keep_trials is TRUE.

Details

The trials are simulated by boin_et_simulate and the OBD is selected by boin_et_select_obd; see there for the rules, and for how they differ from those of 'boinet' unless boinet_compatible is TRUE. The defaults of the OBD selection are those of boinet::boinet(): observed response rates, and the admissible dose with the highest response rate up to the estimated MTD.

References

Takeda, K., Taguri, M. and Morita, S. (2018). BOIN-ET: Bayesian optimal interval design for dose finding based on both efficacy and toxicity outcomes. Pharmaceutical Statistics, 17(4), 383-395. doi:10.1002/pst.1864

Yamaguchi, Y., Takeda, K. and Maruo, K. (2025). boinet: An R Package for Bayesian Optimal Interval Design for Dose Finding Based on Both Efficacy and Toxicity Outcomes. The R Journal, 17(2), 15-34. doi:10.32614/RJ-2025-012

See also

sim_boin_et_multi, boin_et_simulate, boin_et_select_obd

Examples

# Scenario 1 of Takeda et al. (2018)
oc <- sim_boin_et(
  target = 0.30, target_resp = 0.60,
  p_true = c(0.05, 0.15, 0.25, 0.30, 0.35, 0.40),
  p_resp = c(0.05, 0.35, 0.55, 0.65, 0.75, 0.70),
  n_cohort = 12, cohort_size = 3, n_trials = 1000, seed = 123
)
oc
#> BOIN-ET operating characteristics
#>   target DLT rate      : 0.3
#>   target response rate : 0.6
#>   trials               : 1000
#>   cohorts              : 12 of size 3
#>   max sample size      : 36
#>   lambda1 / lambda2    : 0.14 / 0.35
#>   eta1                 : 0.48
#>   OBD selection        : max_resp with observed response rates
#> 
#>                        DL1  DL2  DL3  DL4  DL5  DL6 Total / No OBD
#> True DLT rate (%)      5.0 15.0 25.0 30.0 35.0 40.0               
#> True response rate (%) 5.0 35.0 55.0 65.0 75.0 70.0               
#> OBD selected (%)       1.7 17.0 47.4 26.5  6.1  0.3            1.0
#> Patients treated       3.5  9.1 14.4  7.0  1.7  0.2           35.9
#> Patients with DLT      0.2  1.4  3.6  2.2  0.6  0.1            8.0
#> Patients with response 0.2  3.1  7.9  4.6  1.2  0.1           17.3
#> 
#> Trials stopped early: 1%

# The same trials under the scoring utility
sim_boin_et(
  target = 0.30, target_resp = 0.60,
  p_true = c(0.05, 0.15, 0.25, 0.30, 0.35, 0.40),
  p_resp = c(0.05, 0.35, 0.55, 0.65, 0.75, 0.70),
  n_cohort = 12, cohort_size = 3, n_trials = 1000,
  obd_method = "utility_scoring", seed = 123
)$sel_percent
#>  DL1  DL2  DL3  DL4  DL5  DL6 
#>  2.1 16.7 39.7 30.5  9.4  0.6
